definitions.gloss: Japanese text; writing in Japanese; Japanese-language document
definitions.explanation: Text written in Japanese, as opposed to text in other languages. Used especially in translation and document contexts.

examples.japanese: {和文|わぶん}を{英文|えいぶん}に{訳|やく}す。
examples.english: To translate Japanese text into English.

examples.japanese: {契約書|けいやくしょ}は{和文|わぶん}と{英文|えいぶん}の{両方|りょうほう}で{作成|さくせい}する。
examples.english: The contract will be prepared in both Japanese and English.

examples.japanese: {和文|わぶん}タイプライターは、かつて{日本|にほん}の{事務所|じむしょ}で{広|ひろ}く{使|つか}われていた。
examples.english: Japanese-script typewriters were once widely used in Japanese offices.

notes:
USAGE:
Commonly used in translation work and official documents. The counterpart {英文|えいぶん} means "English text." The pattern ～{文|ぶん} can be used with other language prefixes: {仏文|ふつぶん} (French text), {独文|どくぶん} (German text).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {和文|わぶん}{英訳|えいやく} (Japanese-to-English translation)
- {和文|わぶん}タイプ (Japanese typing)
- {英和|えいわ}・{和英|わえい} (English-Japanese / Japanese-English)
